/-!
# Erdős Problem 923

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/923](https://www.erdosproblems.com/923)
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (1969), 27-35.
- [Ro77] Rödl, V., *On the chromatic number of subgraphs of a given graph*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1977), 370-371.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos923

open SimpleGraph

/--
Is it true that, for every $k$, there is some $f(k)$ such that if $G$ has chromatic number
$\geq f(k)$ then $G$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number $\geq k$?

This is true, as shown by Rödl [Ro77].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos923.lean"]
theorem erdos_923 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) (n : ℕ),
    ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph V, k ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
    ∃ H ≤ G, n ≤ H.chromaticNumber ∧ H.CliqueFree 3 := by
  sorry

end Erdos923

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies the threshold after the vertex type and permits infinite graphs, whereas the source's finite formulation asks for a threshold uniform over graphs. Erdős's original wording also uses χ(G) > f(n), rather than Lean's non-strict threshold.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Instantiate the Lean statement on ULift ℕ. Every finite graph embeds there with additional isolated vertices; increasing the threshold to exclude empty domains allows the resulting subgraph to be pulled back without reducing its chromatic number. This supplies a threshold uniform over finite graphs. Conversely, graph-colouring compactness gives finite subgraphs witnessing failure of any finite colouring, so a uniform finite-graph threshold implies the all-types statement. Strict and non-strict existential thresholds are interchanged by increasing the threshold by one. The complete equivalence with the original finite formulation is proved independently as Review923.statement_iff_original_finite in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, without using the theorem under review.

reformulations.difference: The witness H ≤ G is a spanning subgraph on the same vertex type, while the source permits arbitrary subgraphs, including vertex deletion.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Extend an arbitrary subgraph to the full vertex set by adding isolated vertices. This preserves triangle-freeness and cannot decrease the chromatic number, so it preserves the required lower bound even for empty subgraphs. Conversely, every spanning subgraph is an ordinary subgraph. Review923.hasTF_iff_subgraph proves this exact equivalence for every vertex type and every n, including zero.
